name: AMD Instinct MI350X
memory_bandwidth_basis: '8 TB/s' per the AMD spec table, which lists 'Memory Clock 8 GHz' on an 8192-bit interface. AMD does not publish the arithmetic; treat as 'up to 8 TB/s' vendor figure. AUDIT VERIFIED: 8192-bit x 8 Gb/s per pin / 8 = 8,000 GB/s, which reconciles exactly with AMD's printed figure. (The generic 'HBM3E = 5.0 Gbps' assumption that a mechanical audit would apply gives 5,120 GB/s and is wrong for this part: MI350-series HBM3E runs at 8 Gb/s per pin, and AMD's own spec table lists 'Memory Clock 8 GHz'.)
notes:
Air-cooled sibling of the MI355X. Same CDNA4 silicon, same 288 GB HBM3E, same 8 TB/s, same 8192-bit interface, same 185B transistors, same 8 XCDs / 256 CUs / 16,384 SPs / 1024 matrix cores. It differs ONLY in clock and power: 2200 MHz and 1000W (passive OAM) versus the MI355X's 2400 MHz and 1400W (passive & active).

AMD's own MI355X brochure explains the split: MI355X's higher power budget lets it 'sustain higher performance over time, minimizing throttling and maximizing throughput during prolonged or intensive workloads'. So the real difference is sustained, not burst.

Same eight-die caveat: 288 GB is one package address space across 8 XCDs, not multiple devices.

Compute ratio to MI355X is 2300/2500 = 0.92 on FP16 matrix, matching the 2200/2400 = 0.917 clock ratio exactly - consistent with the same die.

Two fp16 entries on purpose: 144.2 TFLOPS is the VECTOR path, 2300 TFLOPS is the MATRIX path. TF32 is software-emulated on CDNA4 (AMD footnote), so there is no native TF32 figure to carry over from MI300X. Sparse figures are exactly 2x dense. MXFP6/MXFP4 at 9200 PFLOPs are the headline inference datatypes and are quoted without a sparse companion.

7 scale-up Infinity Fabric links at 153 GB/s (product page; the MI355X datasheet gives the more precise 153.6) plus one 128 GB/s scale-out link. ROCm LLVM target gfx950.
